{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Metric Lipschitz lexicographic bandits without tradeoff side information\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{ONX\_\allowbreak{}LEX\_\allowbreak{}LIPSCHITZ\_\allowbreak{}UNKNOWN}



Online learning and bandits



Expected coordinate regret without a tradeoff envelope, quantified by primary-tie metric entropy and regular packing growth.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Lexicographic bandit regret; task family: Online bandit



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Stochastic subgaussian; operation: Two coordinate reward vector; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Private randomness allowed



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} mode: Expectation; quantifier: Algorithm before instance



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} measure: N arm pull; measure: N reward coordinate



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize simultaneous coordinate regret for a two-objective lexicographic stochastic bandit without a supplied tradeoff envelope.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


The public arm space \AtlasInlineMath{(\mathcal X,D)} is a nonempty compact metric space with diameter at most one. The two means take values in [0,1] and are 1-Lipschitz. Compactness ensures the lexicographic optimum exists.



There are two fixed reward means \AtlasInlineMath{\mu^1,\mu^2} taking values in \AtlasInlineMath{[0,1]}. The primary optimum set is \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal X_1^*=\arg\max_x\mu^1(x)}, and a lexicographic optimum \AtlasInlineMath{x^*} maximizes \AtlasInlineMath{\mu^2} over that set. Primary ties are permitted.



The local tradeoff is \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_* =\inf\{\lambda\ge0:\mu^2(x)-\mu^2(x^*)\le\lambda[\mu^1(x^*)-\mu^1(x)]\ \forall x\}}. No value or upper bound for \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_*} is supplied. The same policy must handle all admissible means without such side information.



The local tradeoff can be infinite on compact infinite spaces. The main no-envelope guarantees hold on this class and their lower bounds also hold on the finite-tradeoff subclass.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


At round \AtlasInlineMath{t}, choose an arm \AtlasInlineMath{X_t} using the past and an independent random seed; then observe both coordinates \AtlasInlineMath{(Y_t^1,Y_t^2)}. Each coordinate is conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean: \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E[\exp(\theta(Y_t^i-\mu^i(X_t)))\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},X_t]\le\exp(\theta^2/2)}. Independence between coordinates is not required. There is no feedback for unselected arms and no sample reuse interface.



The horizon and metric are public. A measurable maximal-net oracle, given a nonempty compact subset U and r>0, returns a finite inclusion-maximal r-separated subset. Its computational cost is not charged as a reward observation. Mean functions, primary ties, and near-optimality packing parameters are hidden; the policy uses no tradeoff envelope.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


The output is the sequence of selected arms. One policy must control both objective regrets against the same lexicographic optimum.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


Define \AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_i(x)=\mu^i(x^*)-\mu^i(x)} and signed coordinate regret \AtlasInlineMath{R_i(T)=\sum_{t=1}^T\Delta_i(X_t)}. The simultaneous expected criterion is \AtlasInlineMath{\max_{i\le2}\mathbb E R_i(T)}. The secondary regret can be negative, so the maximum is taken after each expectation.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


There is one arm pull and two scalar reward observations per round, so the fixed horizon is \AtlasInlineMath{T}, the pull count is \AtlasInlineMath{T}, and the number of observed reward coordinates is \AtlasInlineMath{2T}. Computation and storage are unrestricted.



Metric-net computation and reward samples are separate resources. The comparison is information theoretic and does not charge the net construction.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


All measurable randomized causal policies may use T, the metric, and the declared maximal-net interface. The upper policy is independent of the tradeoff and of the near-optimality packing parameters.




\AtlasMath{\forall\nu:\quad\max_{i\le2}\mathbb E_\nu R_i(T)\le r}




The supremum is over fixed Lipschitz means and admissible conditional reward laws on the specified public metric space.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_horizon



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{T}: Horizon \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{T\ge2} integer.



\AtlasInlineMath{(\mathcal X,D)}: Public compact metric arm space \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal X)\le1}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_*}: Unknown local tradeoff \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_*\in[0,\infty]}.



\AtlasInlineMath{S}: Compact tie component in the anchor-plus-tie regimes \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{S\ne\varnothing}, \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{diam}(S)\le1/4}.



\AtlasInlineMath{a}: Anchor arm \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal X=\{a\}\cup S}, \AtlasInlineMath{D(a,z)=1} for z in S.



\AtlasInlineMath{d_p}: Packing-growth exponent \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d_p\ge0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{Z}: Packing-profile size coefficient \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{Z\ge1}.



\AtlasInlineMath{c_-,c_+}: Regular metric packing and covering constants \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{c_-,c_+>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{r_0}: Maximum radius in regular metric growth assumptions \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<r_0\le1/16}.



\AtlasInlineMath{r_s}: Dyadic radius for the entropy frontier \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{s\ge0} integer, \AtlasInlineMath{r_s>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{r_s=2^{-s-4}}



\AtlasInlineMath{s_T}: Final dyadic entropy scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{s_T\in\mathbb N}.



\AtlasInlineMath{s_T=\lceil\log_2(16T)\rceil+2}



\AtlasInlineMath{M_s}: Tie-space packing number \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{M_s\ge1}.



\AtlasInlineMath{M_s=\operatorname{Pack}(S,r_s)}



\AtlasInlineMath{\Psi_T^\infty(S)}: Critical entropy regret scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\Psi_T^\infty(S)>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\Psi_T^\infty(S)=T\max_{0\le s\le s_T}\min\{r_s,(M_s/T)^{1/3}\}}
